name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q01 - Types of redox reactions and Stock notation

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements based on the concepts of redox reactions:

  1. All decomposition reactions are redox reactions because they involve the breakdown of a compound into simpler components.
  2. In the reaction \(2\mathrm{HgCl_2(aq)} + \mathrm{SnCl_2(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Hg_2Cl_2(s)} + \mathrm{SnCl_4(aq)}\), mercuric chloride is reduced while stannous chloride is simultaneously oxidised.
  3. According to Stock notation, \(\mathrm{HAuCl_4}\) and \(\mathrm{MnO_2}\) are represented as \(\mathrm{HAu(III)Cl_4}\) and \(\mathrm{Mn(IV)O_2}\), respectively.
  4. Among the halogens in Group 17, oxidising power increases down the group from fluorine to iodine.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A reaction is a redox reaction only if there is a change in the oxidation number of at least two interacting species (or disproportionation of one species). In Stock notation, the oxidation state of a metal is indicated by a Roman numeral in parentheses immediately after the metal symbol.

Step 2: Evaluation of Decomposition Reactions
For a decomposition reaction to be a redox reaction, at least one of the products must be in the elemental state (or undergo a change in oxidation number). A counterexample is the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate: \(\mathrm{CaCO_3(s)} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{CaO(s)} + \mathrm{CO_2(g)}\), where the oxidation numbers of \(\mathrm{Ca}\) (\(+2\)), \(\mathrm{C}\) (\(+4\)), and \(\mathrm{O}\) (\(-2\)) remain unchanged. Hence, not all decomposition reactions are redox reactions, making the first proposition incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reaction Between Mercuric Chloride and Stannous Chloride
In \(2\mathrm{HgCl_2(aq)} + \mathrm{SnCl_2(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Hg_2Cl_2(s)} + \mathrm{SnCl_4(aq)}\), the oxidation number of mercury decreases from \(+2\) in \(\mathrm{HgCl_2}\) to \(+1\) in \(\mathrm{Hg_2Cl_2}\) (reduction), while the oxidation number of tin increases from \(+2\) in \(\mathrm{SnCl_2}\) to \(+4\) in \(\mathrm{SnCl_4}\) (oxidation). Thus, the second proposition is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Stock Notation Representations
In \(\mathrm{HAuCl_4}\), taking \(\mathrm{H} = +1\) and \(\mathrm{Cl} = -1\), the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{Au}\) is \(+1 + x + 4(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3\), so it is written as \(\mathrm{HAu(III)Cl_4}\). In \(\mathrm{MnO_2}\), taking \(\mathrm{O} = -2\), the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{Mn}\) is \(x + 2(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +4\), so it is written as \(\mathrm{Mn(IV)O_2}\). Thus, the third proposition is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Halogen Oxidising Power and Final Conclusion
The power of halogens as oxidising agents decreases down Group 17 from fluorine to iodine (\(\mathrm{F_2} > \mathrm{Cl_2} > \mathrm{Br_2} > \mathrm{I_2}\)). Therefore, the fourth proposition is incorrect. In total, two propositions are correct and two are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q02 - Redox titrations and balancing ionic equations

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding redox titrations and balanced redox equations:

  1. In redox titrations, permanganate ion (\(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\)) acts as a self-indicator, whereas dichromate ion (\(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\)) requires an external indicator such as diphenylamine.
  2. In iodometric titration using starch and thiosulphate, liberated iodine oxidises thiosulphate ions (\(\mathrm{S_2O_3^{2-}}\)) to tetrathionate ions (\(\mathrm{S_4O_6^{2-}}\)).
  3. In the balanced ionic equation for the reaction of \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\) with \(\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}\) in acidic medium to give \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) and \(\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}\), \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\) reacts with \(3\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}\) and \(8\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{H^+}\).
  4. When \(\mathrm{Pb_3O_4}\) reacts with \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\), the \(\mathrm{PbO_2}\) component oxidises \(\mathrm{NO_3^-}\) to \(\mathrm{NO_2}\) gas in a redox reaction.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Redox titrations detect the equivalence point either through an intensely coloured self-indicator, an external redox indicator, or a starch–iodine complex. Balancing redox equations in acidic medium requires equalising the total increase and decrease in oxidation numbers and balancing charges with \(\mathrm{H^+}\) and atoms with \(\mathrm{H_2O}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Redox Indicators
Permanganate ion (\(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\)) is intensely purple and produces a lasting pink tinge just past the equivalence point at concentrations as low as \(10^{-6}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), acting as a self-indicator. Dichromate ion (\(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\)) does not show a sharp auto-colour change at the endpoint and instead oxidises diphenylamine immediately after the equivalence point to produce an intense blue colour. Thus, the first proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Iodine–Thiosulphate Titration
In the reaction \(\mathrm{I_2(aq)} + 2\mathrm{S_2O_3^{2-}(aq)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{I^-(aq)} + \mathrm{S_4O_6^{2-}(aq)}\), iodine is reduced from \(0\) to \(-1\), while the average oxidation state of sulphur increases from \(+2\) in \(\mathrm{S_2O_3^{2-}}\) to \(+2.5\) in \(\mathrm{S_4O_6^{2-}}\). Thus, iodine oxidises thiosulphate to tetrathionate, making the second proposition correct.

Step 4: Balancing the Dichromate–Sulphite Reaction
In \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}(aq)} + \mathrm{SO_3^{2-}(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cr^{3+}(aq)} + \mathrm{SO_4^{2-}(aq)}\), chromium decreases from \(+6\) to \(+3\) (a decrease of \(3\) per \(\mathrm{Cr}\) atom, or \(6\) per \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\) ion), while sulphur increases from \(+4\) to \(+6\) (an increase of \(2\) per \(\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}\) ion). Equalising electron transfer requires \(3\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}\) per \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\):
\(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}(aq)} + 3\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}(aq)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr^{3+}(aq)} + 3\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}(aq)}\).
Balancing the net ionic charge (\(-2 + 3(-2) = -8\) on the left; \(2(+3) + 3(-2) = 0\) on the right) requires adding \(8\mathrm{H^+}\) on the left and \(4\mathrm{H_2O}\) on the right:
\(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}(aq)} + 3\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}(aq)} + 8\mathrm{H^+(aq)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr^{3+}(aq)} + 3\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}(aq)} + 4\mathrm{H_2O(l)}\).
Thus, the third proposition is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of the Reaction of \(\mathrm{Pb_3O_4}\) with \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) and Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{Pb_3O_4}\) is a stoichiometric mixture of \(2\text{ mol}\) \(\mathrm{PbO}\) and \(1\text{ mol}\) \(\mathrm{PbO_2}\). Because \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) itself is an oxidising agent, \(\mathrm{PbO_2}\) remains passive toward \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) and only the basic oxide \(\mathrm{PbO}\) undergoes an acid–base reaction: \(\mathrm{Pb_3O_4} + 4\mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2} + \mathrm{PbO_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}\). No \(\mathrm{NO_2}\) gas is formed. Thus, the fourth proposition is incorrect. In total, three statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q03 - Standard electrode potentials and galvanic cells

questiontext.text:
Using the following standard reduction potentials at \(298\text{ K}\):

\(E^\circ(\mathrm{Li^+/Li}) = -3.05\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}/Zn}) = -0.76\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{H^+/H_2}) = 0.00\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}) = +0.34\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Ag^+/Ag}) = +0.80\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Au^{3+}/Au}) = +1.40\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{F_2/F^-}) = +2.87\text{ V}\).

Evaluate the following four statements:

  1. When a metallic zinc strip is placed in an aqueous \(\mathrm{Cu(NO_3)_2}\) solution, the blue colour disappears because \(\mathrm{Zn}\) is oxidised to \(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) is reduced to \(\mathrm{Cu(s)}\).
  2. Among the given species, \(\mathrm{Li(s)}\) is the strongest reducing agent and \(\mathrm{F_2(g)}\) is the strongest oxidising agent.
  3. Metallic silver (\(\mathrm{Ag}\)) and gold (\(\mathrm{Au}\)) do not displace \(\mathrm{H_2(g)}\) from hydrochloric acid because their positive standard reduction potentials make them weaker reducing agents than the \(\mathrm{H^+/H_2}\) couple.
  4. In a galvanic cell operating via \(\mathrm{Zn(s)} + 2\mathrm{Ag^+(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn^{2+}(aq)} + 2\mathrm{Ag(s)}\), the zinc electrode acts as the anode and is negatively charged.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Standard reduction potentials at \(298\text{ K}\) are: \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Li^+/Li}) = -3.05\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}/Zn}) = -0.76\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{H^+/H_2}) = 0.00\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}) = +0.34\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Ag^+/Ag}) = +0.80\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Au^{3+}/Au}) = +1.40\text{ V}\), and \(E^\circ(\mathrm{F_2/F^-}) = +2.87\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
All \(E^\circ\) values represent standard reduction potentials (\(\text{Oxidised form} + n\mathrm{e^-} \rightarrow \text{Reduced form}\)) at unit concentration (or \(1\text{ atm}\) for gases) and \(298\text{ K}\). By convention, a negative \(E^\circ\) indicates a stronger reducing agent than \(\mathrm{H^+/H_2}\), whereas a positive \(E^\circ\) indicates a weaker reducing agent than \(\mathrm{H^+/H_2}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. Cell potential for spontaneity: \(\Delta E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} > 0\).
2. In a galvanic cell, oxidation occurs at the negatively charged anode, which releases electrons into the external circuit, and reduction occurs at the positively charged cathode.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
First, for zinc placed in \(\mathrm{Cu(NO_3)_2(aq)}\), the reaction \(\mathrm{Zn(s)} + \mathrm{Cu^{2+}(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn^{2+}(aq)} + \mathrm{Cu(s)}\) has \(\Delta E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +0.34\text{ V} - (-0.76\text{ V}) = +1.10\text{ V} > 0\). Thus, \(\mathrm{Zn}\) is oxidised to colourless \(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}\) and blue \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) ions are reduced to metallic \(\mathrm{Cu}\), causing the blue colour to disappear.
Second, a lower (more negative) \(E^\circ\) corresponds to a stronger reducing agent, while a higher (more positive) \(E^\circ\) corresponds to a stronger oxidising agent. Since \(\mathrm{Li^+/Li}\) has the most negative \(E^\circ\) (\(-3.05\text{ V}\)), \(\mathrm{Li(s)}\) is the strongest reducing agent; since \(\mathrm{F_2/F^-}\) has the most positive \(E^\circ\) (\(+2.87\text{ V}\)), \(\mathrm{F_2(g)}\) is the strongest oxidising agent.
Third, both \(\mathrm{Ag^+/Ag}\) (\(+0.80\text{ V}\)) and \(\mathrm{Au^{3+}/Au}\) (\(+1.40\text{ V}\)) have positive \(E^\circ\) values relative to \(\mathrm{H^+/H_2}\) (\(0.00\text{ V}\)). Hence, \(\mathrm{Ag}\) and \(\mathrm{Au}\) are weaker reducing agents than \(\mathrm{H_2}\) and cannot reduce \(\mathrm{H^+}\) from \(\mathrm{HCl}\) to \(\mathrm{H_2(g)}\).
Fourth, in the cell reaction \(\mathrm{Zn(s)} + 2\mathrm{Ag^+(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn^{2+}(aq)} + 2\mathrm{Ag(s)}\), \(\mathrm{Zn}\) undergoes oxidation (\(\mathrm{Zn} \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn^{2+}} + 2\mathrm{e^-}\)), so the zinc electrode is the anode and acquires a negative charge as electrons are released onto it.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
All potential differences and sign conventions are consistent with the standard electrode potential series. Each of the four propositions is scientifically accurate. Therefore, all four statements are correct.
